judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Except as to such modifications as are described in this letter' calls the document a letter when it is headed a memorandum, and the modifications are not enumerated here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Point Two then rewrites paragraph (e) wholesale, so the assurance that 2-E.2 'applies fully' is immediately qualified in a way that has to be reconciled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Will begin to apply the principle' is not a commitment to apply it, and the two exceptions (over 250 miles, more than two stops) are stated in the alternative without saying who measures them.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-E.2(e) requires transfer points within the Metropolitan Area and (e)(1) requires through-driving to Albany and other designated cities, both of which this rewriting displaces.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A transfer point is a location where...' is a careful functional definition, and the selection is 'subject to the agreement of the Union' with a stated fallback.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-E.2(e) sends transfer-point disputes to the Impartial Chairman for final and binding decision, while this clause sends them to Section 16 generally — two different fora for the same dispute.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'But no such transfer point will be farther from Columbus Circle, except at the choice of The Times, than the destination point' is a double-negative constraint with a discretionary escape.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-E.2(e) requires transfer points within the Metropolitan Area 'as near the limits as practical', which cannot be squared with a point more than 150 miles out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The two-sided constraint (no farther than 150 miles, no nearer than any transfer point then in use) is precise and the named points are listed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Hightstown clause in the same memorandum eliminates Hightstown as a transfer point, yet it is named here as one in use — a direct internal contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Will be responsible for his load' is a broad allocation of responsibility with only one example of what it includes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-G's shortage machinery and 2-J's default-on-collections rule address related responsibility, but no conflict is evident.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The condition (45 hours or more without a fifth shift) and the consequence (benefit credits as if a fifth shift were worked) are stated precisely, with 'etc.' left open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-H.1 and 13-I.1 measure contributions by shifts actually worked capped at five, so deeming a fifth shift for pension and welfare credit cuts directly against that formula.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Every practical legal means' and 'a substantial sales loss, due to a jurisdictional dispute' are soft, and the whole paragraph is keyed to a January 1, 1974 deadline long past.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-E.2(g) already lets the Publisher discontinue runs on a jurisdictional dispute, and the Farer Runs clause converts Farer runs to direct runs, which this paragraph treats as a fallback.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An agreement 'to meet promptly ... to discuss the feasibility' with an open-ended 'etc.' list; no obligation is created.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 17-D says the parties have bargained and settled terms for the term of the Agreement, which sits against several open commitments to discuss.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Allowance will be made on runs with more than one destination' states no measure for the allowance, leaving the rule incomplete for multi-stop runs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Run Times clause amends 'the phrase 89 miles' to 27 miles in a prior booklet, and 21-D.I.E preserves 'present practice' on running time, so run time is fixed inconsistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text reads 'will be construed clude this stipulation', omitting the verb, and 'the seasonal factor' is explained only by example.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-E.2(h) as written lets a Publisher discontinue over-the-road trucking and employ other carriers at any time, which this stipulation materially restricts for The Times.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The paragraph ends 'the assignments of these men will be changed as follows:' and then stops, so the operative change is not stated in this provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraphs 2 and 3 supply the changes, so the introduction is incomplete on its own but coherent read with them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Will continue in their present form during the term of this Agreement' is definite, though 'present form' is undated and the replacement mechanism is loosely stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-J allows starting-time and day-off changes on four days' notice and 4-B governs how vacated situations are filled, both of which this freeze displaces for two named men.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Vacates for any reason' is broad but clear, and the consequence is stated precisely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4-B requires vacancies to be posted and filled by seniority, whereas this converts the situation to a floor situation automatically.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'As of the last day of this Agreement' effects a change at the very moment the Agreement ends, which is a self-defeating timing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 19 fixes expiration at March 30, 1984, so an obligation taking effect on the last day and continuing 'thereafter' outruns the instrument's term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short conditional prohibition tied to whether work exists.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4-A.2 governs the hiring of extras generally; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise anti-offset amendment keyed to a named plan and a retirement date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-I.1 requires contributions to the joint Pension Fund, and this clause prevents the company plan from offsetting those benefits; consistent in direction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any other life insurance coverage which such employee has or in the future may have' is a general catch-all after the specific NMDU Welfare Fund reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-H establishes the Welfare Fund whose life insurance is expressly named, so the interaction is anticipated rather than conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Restore the full amount ... to which the employee thereafter is entitled, and for which he is enrolled' stacks two conditions on a restoration promise, but the sense is recoverable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-G.1's anti-offset rule is the premise for this restoration; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The declination mechanism, the deadline 'clearly stated on the form' and the medical-examination consequence are all specified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the express complement to 22-G.2(a); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An introductory sentence referring to 'the schedule now in use', an undated external document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-A.1 requires each Publisher to continue the schedules in its last notice to the Union, so this new schedule operates alongside that requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single precise loading figure for two named page sizes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-A.1 caps bundles at 46 pounds and 21-C.2 caps News trucks at 240 loads, but this is a Times-specific figure and does not conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise weight-triggered loading figure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 3 uses a 37-to-46-pound band for stacking height while this uses a 42-pound threshold for count, so two different weight thresholds govern the same bundles.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It says trailers load 'to a maximum of six high' and then sets five high for 37-to-46-pound bundles (printed '87 to 46'), and allows the six-high maximum to be exceeded for 'a reasonable number of bundles'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-A.1 caps bundle weight at 46 pounds, which lines up with the top of this band, but the Saturday-night exception has no counterpart elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise waiver of collection of an identified judgment by amount, action number and date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 3 preserves the right to seek damages for future incidents, and 16-N/16-K supply the underlying enforcement scheme; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Will develop a stipulation' is a soft procedural commitment, and the filing date given (July 29) differs from the grant date (July 9) without explanation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 1 promises not to collect the judgment, and this paragraph goes further to vacate it; consistent in direction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall not prejudice The Times' right to seek and collect damages ... with respect to any future incident' is broad but clearly reserved.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-K empowers the Boards to impose damages for violations, which this reservation preserves; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise identification of the award, the arbitrator, the work stoppage and the sum.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Satisfaction of Damage Award letter says that after six payments The News will not 'under any circumstances' require additional payments, which cannot be reconciled with paying the full $177,844.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise instalment amount and commencement date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: At $1,250 a month the stated principal would take over eleven years, yet the companion letter forgives the balance after six payments — a direct conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line waiver of interest; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the instalment schedule and the forgiveness letter.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Other relevant factors' is an open-ended catch-all, and the clause requires only a meeting to review.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Satisfaction of Damage Award letter ties forgiveness to six payments while this ties a review to six months after the first payment, two different six-based triggers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'More favorable terms or treatment with respect to the payment or disposition called for by an arbitration award or judicial decree' is a comparison the clause gives no method for making.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Pension/Welfare parity letter contains a similar most-favoured-union commitment with carve-outs, and the forgiveness letter already caps the Union's exposure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise commitment tied to a numbered action.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with paragraph 1's payment scheme; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The provisions against strikes and disruptions of orderly relationships' names no provision, and 'disruptions of orderly relationships' has no counterpart anywhere in the Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-N prohibits strikes, lockouts and other cessations of work but says nothing about 'disruptions of orderly relationships', so the acceleration trigger is broader than any operative no-strike clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any major change in its operations which has an impact on a significant number of its NMDU employees' stacks two undefined thresholds, softened only by a single parenthetical example.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-M.3 forbids any change in condition without the other party's prior consent, so a mere thirty days' notice regime is hard to reconcile with a consent requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It fixes the meaning of 16-M by reference to an arbitrator's unwritten oral opinion and to three points from a 1971 award in a different case between different parties.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-M.3 and 16-M.4 are the operative change-of-conditions rules, and this memorandum makes their content depend on documents outside the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Every memorandum, letter agreement or side agreement shall be continued ... and deemed updated' is a sweeping catch-all, and 'deemed updated' is given no content at all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 21-B.4 and 21-G.3 declare particular side agreements expired, and 21-D.VIII supersedes all other agreements relating to Newspoint, so this blanket continuation cannot be squared with them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'This Supplementary Agreement is within the terms of the current collective bargaining agreement' is an assertion of consistency rather than a rule, and the memorandum is dated before the October 26, 1981 execution.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its own ¶4 guarantees against starting-time changes, which is not 'within the terms' of 5-J, so the self-description is contradicted by the substance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The arithmetic is spelled out (two situations, one of five nights and one of four days plus one night, eleven shifts total), which is precise if unusual.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-A's Floor Operations clause sets a one-employee floor minimum and ¶3 an 81-hire minimum, so several manning commitments stack at Carlstadt.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Including but not limited to' opens the assignment list, while the last sentence makes one task exclusive to the utility man — a general grant and a specific exclusivity in one paragraph.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 6-B bars foremen from performing Section 2 operations beyond limits and 22-A's Control Room clause allocates console work, so the utility man's exclusive task overlaps existing allocations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Aleo Men', 'normal daily operation' and 'provided all areas are properly manned' are all undefined, and 'normal reduction in press utilization' is vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly preserves 'the obligation of The Times to hire from the shape in priority order in accordance with the Agreement', acknowledging tension with 4-A.2's hiring sequence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All regular situation holders as of the date of this agreement are guaranteed against a change in their present starting times' is absolute, and the qualifier refers to 'the named individuals' when none are named.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-J expressly permits the Publisher to change starting times on four days' notice, and 20-E.7 gives discretion over starting times on a Bulldog phase-out — a direct conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The half-hour premium and its exception are stated precisely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-L directs the parties to negotiate travel-time compensation with a Board fallback, and this supplies one instance of it; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line delivery obligation fixed as of the signing date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-J requires a starting-time and days-off list to the chapel chairman, and the posting letter adds job descriptions; all consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Blue Goose' is defined parenthetically as a passenger vehicle and the obligation is tied to two named men's job.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-K requires the Publisher to furnish all delivery equipment, which this specific commitment implements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'As it does during the week' fixes the standard by reference to existing practice, which is undated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-E.2(e)(1) requires through-driving to Albany by covered employees, which this Saturday extension tracks; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A concrete monthly commitment with a stated purpose.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 14-C addresses discharge for a bad driving record, which DOT examinations bear on; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Such route shall be filed by in-shop bidding' reads 'filed' where 'filled' is meant, but the commitment is otherwise precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4-B requires posting and filling of new situations by seniority among regular situation holders, which in-shop bidding tracks.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Including, but not limited to' opens the list of postable items, and 'their past practice' is undated for one party and absent for the other.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The closing sentence disclaims any effect on rights under the Agreement, and 5-J already requires a starting-time and days-off list, so the two overlap without conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Whatever increase, however formulated' is qualified by two exceptions — productivity exchange 'as determined to the Union's reasonable satisfaction' and diversion 'from the negotiated pattern package' — neither of which is defined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-H.1 and 13-I.1 fix contribution percentages for the term, and 13-A.2 allocates a $6.00 fringe, so an open-ended parity promise sits against fixed contribution rates.
